candidates.bio: Republican elementary school teacher in Los Angeles Unified with more than 25 years of experience who also ran for this seat in 2024.
candidates.platform: Her site calls for lowering costs (reducing gas taxes, regulations and small-business taxes), auditing state spending, funding Prop 36 and fighting fentanyl and human trafficking, smaller classes and trades training, reducing homelessness through rehabilitation and mental health facilities, and protecting parental rights.

46.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent (Assembly Budget chair) took 66.2% in the primary; State Navigate rates it Solid D.
46.summary: Democrat Jesse Gabriel (west San Fernando Valley) faces a rematch with 2024 Republican opponent Tracey Schroeder; not competitive.

candidates.name: Greg Wallis
candidates.bio: Republican Assemblymember for the 47th District since 2022, seeking a third term; a former district director and chief district advisor to Assemblymember Chad Mayes.
candidates.platform: His campaign site says he is focused on lowering costs for working people, protecting residents from crime, and cleaning up corruption in Sacramento, with an emphasis on affordability and economic opportunity for the Coachella Valley and Inland Empire.

candidates.name: Leila Namvar
candidates.bio: Democrat from La Quinta who works as a public arts program analyst for the City of Indio and is a labor representative and union leader; an Iranian immigrant and mother with no prior elected office.
candidates.platform: Her campaign says she will fight for working families by taking on corporate greed, advocating for affordable housing, pushing for good-paying jobs, and expanding access to education and quality healthcare.

47.likely_winner_basis: Lean/uncertain: the two Democrats combined for 51.8% of the primary vote to Wallis's 48.1%, and State Navigate's model rates the seat Likely D (90.7%); but Wallis is a two-term incumbent in a near-even district and could hold on.
47.summary: One of the more competitive Assembly races in Southern California: Republican incumbent Greg Wallis (Palm Springs / Coachella Valley / Yucca Valley), who won by narrow margins in 2022 and 2024, faces Democrat Leila Namvar, a union organizer and state civil servant. Wallis fell short of a majority in the June primary.

candidates.name: Blanca Rubio
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 48th District since 2016, a former 16-year schoolteacher and Baldwin Park Unified School District trustee who chairs the Assembly Governmental Organization Committee.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site lists education and youth, housing and homelessness, domestic violence prevention, public safety, healthcare, climate, and consumer protection among her legislative focus areas.

candidates.name: Dan T. Tran
candidates.bio: Republican real estate professional from the Glendora area and the 2024 runner-up in this district.

48.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 65.3% in the two-candidate primary; State Navigate rates it Solid D.
48.summary: Democrat Blanca Rubio (San Gabriel Valley: Baldwin Park, West Covina, Azusa) faces a rematch with 2024 Republican opponent Dan Tran; not competitive.

candidates.name: Mike Fong
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 49th District since a 2022 special election, previously a Los Angeles Community College District trustee and Los Angeles city official, who chairs the Assembly Higher Education Committee.
candidates.platform: His campaign site emphasizes creating good-paying local jobs, addressing climate change and homelessness, safe neighborhoods, and support for local schools and small businesses.

candidates.name: Long David Liu
candidates.bio: Republican attorney with more than 20 years of practice who describes his work as advocating for underserved, multi-ethnic communities.
candidates.platform: His campaign centers on backing police and holding offenders accountable, 'humane but effective' homelessness solutions, opposing tax increases and regulatory burdens on businesses, and a merit-based school system with greater parental involvement.

49.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 68.2% in the two-candidate primary; State Navigate rates it Solid D.
49.summary: Democrat Mike Fong (Alhambra/Monterey Park/San Gabriel) faces Republican attorney Long David Liu; not competitive.

candidates.name: Robert Garcia
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 50th District since December 2024, a longtime math and science teacher and school administrator who served on the Etiwanda School District board from 2016 to 2024.

candidates.name: Victoria Viveros Mageno
candidates.bio: Republican member of the Cucamonga School District Board of Trustees since 2020 (currently vice president) with more than 20 years in women's leadership ministry at Victory Outreach Chino.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site calls for stopping tax hikes and wasteful spending, fully funding Proposition 36 and supporting law enforcement, requiring voter ID, improving education and workforce opportunities, and addressing homelessness by confronting mental illness and addiction.

50.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 58.2% in a three-way primary (Republican 38.7%, NPP 3.1%); State Navigate rates it Solid D (99.4%).
50.summary: First-term Democrat Robert Garcia (Rancho Cucamonga / Fontana area) faces Republican school board trustee Victoria Viveros Mageno; a single-digit-lean seat on paper but the incumbent is favored.

candidates.name: Rick Chavez Zbur
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 51st District since 2022 and Assembly Democratic Caucus Chair, an environmental and civil rights attorney who previously led Equality California.
candidates.platform: His re-election site prioritizes protecting Medi-Cal and lowering healthcare costs, defending reproductive freedom, holding serious offenders accountable, protecting immigrant communities, climate action, and affordability.

candidates.name: Colin D. Hernandez
candidates.bio: Democratic digital communications strategist and Los Angeles native who has worked in advocacy on LGBTQ+ rights, tax policy, criminal justice and immigration reform.
candidates.platform: He campaigns on 'CalCare for All' single-payer healthcare, 'Housing for All,' universal childcare, and taxing the top 1% and large corporations, and says he refuses corporate and super PAC money.

51.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 54.1% in a five-way primary versus 22.1% for Hernandez; Zbur has the party endorsement and a large funding and name-recognition edge.
51.summary: Democrat-vs-Democrat general in a deep-blue Westside/Hollywood district: incumbent Rick Chavez Zbur faces digital strategist Colin D. Hernandez, who edged out two Republicans for the second runoff spot. Not competitive.

candidates.name: Jessica Caloza
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 52nd District since 2024 and Assistant Majority Whip, formerly a Los Angeles Board of Public Works commissioner and deputy chief of staff to Attorney General Rob Bonta.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site lists lowering costs and building affordable housing, strengthening public education, protecting reproductive freedom, expanding middle-class jobs, addressing gun violence, and confronting the climate crisis.

candidates.name: Andrea Lee Anderson
candidates.bio: Republican challenger from a public-service family (her father was a mayor, her mother a Girl Scouts executive).
candidates.platform: Her stated priorities include balancing the state budget, lowering taxes and reducing regulation, expanding school choice, stricter enforcement of existing criminal and sidewalk laws, supporting federal immigration enforcement, and maintaining in-state oil production alongside nuclear power.

52.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 85.8% in the two-candidate primary; State Navigate rates it Solid D.
52.summary: First-term Democrat Jessica Caloza (Echo Park / Eagle Rock / Glendale-adjacent northeast LA) faces Republican Andrea Lee Anderson; not competitive.

candidates.name: Michelle Rodriguez
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 53rd District since 2024 and Assistant Majority Whip, a lifelong Ontario/Pomona-area resident with a background in local public schools and healthcare administration.
candidates.platform: Her 2024 campaign priorities included universal healthcare, homelessness, and education.

candidates.name: Rafaela Romero
candidates.bio: Republican challenger whose ballot designation is special education aide; her site references community food-distribution work.
candidates.platform: Her site emphasizes lowering everyday costs (housing, gas, groceries, utilities), public safety policies that 'hold criminals accountable,' support for parents and access to quality education, and infrastructure investment to improve traffic flow.

53.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 62.3% in the two-candidate primary; State Navigate rates it Solid D (99.7%).
53.summary: First-term Democrat Michelle Rodriguez (Pomona / Ontario / Chino) faces Republican special-education aide Rafaela Romero; not competitive.

candidates.name: Mark Gonzalez
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 54th District since 2024 and Majority Whip, formerly chair of the Los Angeles County Democratic Party.
candidates.platform: His campaign site highlights making community college free, protecting air and water, making housing more affordable, safeguarding abortion rights, and improving support for vulnerable seniors.

54.partisan_lean: 2024 presidential: Harris +43.9; Gonzalez won 56.3% in 2024 (vs. a fellow Democrat)
54.likely_winner_basis: Gonzalez was the only candidate on the primary ballot (99.7%); his opponent qualified as a write-in with 137 votes. Solid D.
54.summary: Democrat Mark Gonzalez (downtown / East Los Angeles) is effectively unopposed: Republican Alexandra Briseno reached the November ballot as a primary write-in with 137 votes and appears on the SoS certified list without a ballot designation.

candidates.name: Isaac G. Bryan
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 55th District since 2021 and a former Assembly Majority Leader who previously ran UCLA's Black Policy Project.
candidates.platform: His campaign plan lists six priorities: putting people first, supporting working families, protecting the environment, reimagining the justice system, housing for all, and creating good-paying jobs.

candidates.name: Ashley M. Brown
candidates.bio: LAUSD psychiatric/school social worker and lifelong Los Angeles resident making her first run for office.
candidates.platform: She names community safety through prevention, women's and mental health access, and education and economic stability as her top issues, framing her approach as investing in prevention over crisis response.

55.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 64.6% in a four-way primary versus 18.9% for Brown; party-endorsed with a large resource advantage.
55.summary: Democrat-vs-Democrat general in a deep-blue Culver City / Baldwin Hills / Mid-City district: incumbent Isaac Bryan faces school social worker Ashley M. Brown. Not competitive.

candidates.name: Lisa Calderon
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 56th District since 2020 who chairs the Assembly Insurance Committee and previously worked in government affairs for Edison International.
candidates.platform: She frames her agenda as helping constituents get ahead, naming food assistance, health care access and K-12 funding as budget priorities and citing minimum-wage increases and lower utility and gas costs; her official site highlights wildfire reform and utility accountability.

candidates.name: Jessica Martinez
candidates.bio: Retired teacher and former Whittier city councilmember and mayor pro tem (2020-2024) with a J.D. from Trinity Law School.
candidates.platform: Her campaign runs on 'Education. Economy. Safety.': supporting charter schools, vouchers and homeschooling options, lower taxes and reduced regulation, and law-and-order policies including support for law enforcement, border security and Second Amendment rights.

56.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 64.1% in the two-candidate primary; State Navigate rates it Solid D (99.8%).
56.summary: Democrat Lisa Calderon (Whittier / Montebello / Hacienda Heights) faces former Whittier councilmember Jessica Martinez (R); not competitive.

candidates.name: Sade Elhawary
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 57th District since 2024, a former high-school teacher, college counselor and Community Coalition organizer who also worked for Mayor Karen Bass.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site's priorities include housing as a human right, healthcare for all, expanding mental health resources, environmental justice, strong public schools, reproductive justice, safe neighborhoods through prevention programs, and protecting immigrants.

candidates.name: Constance Jewel Menzies
candidates.bio: Republican in-home care provider from Los Angeles.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site lists safer neighborhoods, stronger schools, economic opportunity and support for working families and seniors as priorities, without further policy detail.

57.partisan_lean: 2024 presidential: Harris +52.6; Elhawary won 61.1% in 2024 (vs. a fellow Democrat)
57.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 85.7% in the two-candidate primary; State Navigate rates it Solid D.
57.summary: First-term Democrat Sade Elhawary (South Los Angeles) faces Republican Constance Jewel Menzies; not competitive.

candidates.name: Leticia Castillo
candidates.bio: Republican Assemblymember for the 58th District since 2024, a licensed marriage and family therapist from Corona and former Riverside County mental-health clinician who flipped the seat by 596 votes.
candidates.platform: Campaigning under 'Faith, Family, Freedom,' her site lists protecting parental rights, restoring public safety, lowering the cost of living and taxes, protecting Prop 13, opposing abortion, Second Amendment rights and quality education.

candidates.name: Clarissa Cervantes
candidates.bio: Riverside City Councilmember (Ward 2), businesswoman and mother with a master's in urban planning from Cal Poly Pomona; sister of state Sen. Sabrina Cervantes and the 2024 runner-up in this district by 596 votes.
candidates.platform: Her priorities page lists expanding affordable housing and childcare, opposing utility and water-rate increases and warehouse overdevelopment, strengthening wages and local job creation, reducing healthcare costs, and adequate staffing for firefighters and police.

58.partisan_lean: 2024 presidential: Harris +4.0; Castillo (R) won 50.2% in a 2024 upset
58.likely_winner_basis: Cervantes led the incumbent 54.5%-45.5% in the June two-candidate primary and State Navigate rates the seat Very Likely D (94%); still a genuine contest given Castillo's 2024 upset.
58.summary: Rematch of the 2024 upset: freshman Republican Leticia Castillo (Riverside / Corona / Eastvale) faces Riverside councilmember Clarissa Cervantes (D), who lost by 596 votes in 2024 but outpolled Castillo 54.5-45.5 in the primary. The top Democratic flip target in the region: Cervantes had raised about $2.6M to Castillo's roughly $0.9M as of early October, according to the Press-Enterprise, with the state Democratic Party and unions behind Cervantes and the Southern California News Group editorial boards endorsing Castillo.

candidates.name: Phillip Chen
candidates.bio: Republican Assemblymember for the 59th District since 2016, a business owner and former Walnut Valley Unified School District trustee and Los Angeles County reserve sheriff's deputy.
candidates.platform: His re-election site centers on safer neighborhoods, stronger schools and a more affordable California, highlighting fiscal responsibility, public safety and education.

candidates.name: Victor Hernandez
candidates.bio: Green Party account sales manager from Brea, age 34, who has not held elected office.
candidates.platform: Running on 'People Over Corporations' and refusing corporate or PAC money, his site lists affordable housing, healthcare for all, defending communities and protecting natural resources; in a newspaper questionnaire he backed expanding rent control to single-family rentals and raising the renter's tax credit.

59.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 66.3% in the primary against a Green Party candidate with no Democrat on the ballot. State Navigate: Solid R (93%).
59.summary: Republican Phillip Chen (Yorba Linda / Chino Hills / Diamond Bar) faces Green Party candidate Victor Hernandez; no Democrat filed. Not competitive.

candidates.name: Corey A. Jackson
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for the 60th District since 2022, a social worker with a doctorate from California Baptist University who previously served on the Riverside County Board of Education.
candidates.platform: His stated campaign message is breaking cycles of poverty and violence through community investment. Campaign site was offline when checked.

candidates.name: Ed Delgado
candidates.bio: Moreno Valley City Councilmember (District 2, elected 2021) and retired Riverside County assistant sheriff with 25 years in the Sheriff's Department and 10 years in the U.S. Coast Guard.
candidates.platform: His campaign lists public safety, affordability and making California a 'two-party state' as priorities under the slogan 'Common Sense. Safer Streets. Stronger Families,' and he is endorsed by the Riverside, San Bernardino and Orange County sheriffs.

60.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 59.8% in a three-way primary (Republicans combined 40.2%); State Navigate rates it Solid D (99.1%).
60.summary: Democrat Corey Jackson (Moreno Valley / Perris) faces Moreno Valley councilmember Ed Delgado (R); a single-digit-lean seat where the incumbent is favored.

candidates.name: Tina McKinnor
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember (since a 2022 special election) and former California Democratic Party operations director and Assembly chief of staff; chairs the Public Employment and Retirement Committee.
candidates.platform: Her official Assembly materials emphasize public-employee retirement policy and her committee leadership.

candidates.name: Brian Lockwood
candidates.bio: Property-management professional who qualified for the November ballot as a write-in candidate in the June primary.
candidates.platform: Campaign site carries a 'Los Angeles deserves better' message focused on rebuilding the district.

61.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 98.6% of the primary in a Harris +57 district against a write-in opponent.
61.summary: Safe Democratic seat; McKinnor faces only Republican write-in Brian Lockwood, who advanced with 1.4% of the primary vote.

candidates.name: Jose Solache
candidates.bio: First-term incumbent assemblymember and former Lynwood mayor, city councilmember (2013-2024) and Lynwood Unified school board member.
candidates.platform: Priorities listed include economic development, housing affordability, child-care costs and CalFresh enrollment.

candidates.name: Paul Irving Jones
candidates.bio: Retired Marine Corps combat veteran, former Teamsters Local 399 studio driver and LAUSD computer instructor from Lakewood; 2024 runner-up for this seat.
candidates.platform: Campaign lists education reform, housing and government integrity, and health-care reform as top priorities.

62.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 73.1% of the primary in a Harris +29 district; rematch of the 2024 general, which he won 66-34.
62.summary: Safe Democratic seat; a rematch of 2024 between first-term incumbent Solache and Republican Paul Irving Jones.

candidates.name: Natasha Johnson
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since winning the 2025 special election to replace Bill Essayli; small-business owner with 26 years in banking and a Lake Elsinore councilmember (2012-2025) who served three terms as mayor.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include public safety and law-enforcement funding, lowering the cost of living for working families and small businesses, and addressing homelessness through mental-health services and transitional housing.

candidates.name: Kevin Akin
candidates.bio: Retired carpenter, steelworker and hospital steam engineer from Riverside, longtime union member and Peace and Freedom Party leader who advanced as a write-in.
candidates.platform: Campaign calls for expanded access to affordable housing, child care and transportation, free public education from preschool through university, universal medical care, and representation of working people.

63.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 99.3% of the primary in a Trump +13 district; only opponent is a write-in minor-party candidate with 0.7%.
63.summary: Safe Republican seat; Johnson seeks her first full term against Peace and Freedom write-in Kevin Akin, with no Democrat on the ballot.

candidates.name: Blanca Pacheco
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2022 and chair of the Assembly Rules Committee; attorney and former two-term Downey mayor and councilmember.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as housing affordability, public-school funding and public safety.

candidates.name: Raul Ortiz Jr.
candidates.bio: La Mirada resident, ordained minister and pest-control business manager; 2024 runner-up for this seat.
candidates.platform: Campaign emphasizes public-education quality, small-business advocacy, public safety and parental authority.

64.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 66.5% of the primary in a Harris +16 district; she beat Ortiz 62.5-37.5 in 2024.
64.summary: Safe Democratic seat; a rematch of 2024 between Rules Committee chair Pacheco and Republican Raul Ortiz Jr.

incumbent.name: Mike Gipson
incumbent.note: termed out; running for State Board of Equalization

candidates.name: Ayanna Davis
candidates.bio: Vice president of the Compton Unified School District board (elected 2022), former teacher and principal in Watts for 21 years, with a USC doctorate in education; endorsed by the California Legislative Black Caucus.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as support for working families, public safety and support for health-care workers.

candidates.name: Lydia Gutiérrez
candidates.bio: Veteran public-school teacher (Long Beach Unified and Hawthorne districts), former aerospace administrator and former Coastal San Pedro Neighborhood Council member; has run several times for state and LAUSD offices.

65.likely_winner_basis: Led a six-way primary with 46.3% in a Harris +44 district; Democrats combined for about 81% of the primary vote.
65.summary: Open seat (Gipson termed out) in a heavily Democratic South LA County district; Davis is heavily favored over Republican Lydia Gutiérrez.

incumbent.name: Al Muratsuchi
incumbent.note: termed out; ran unsuccessfully for Superintendent of Public Instruction

candidates.name: Sara Deen
candidates.bio: Family dentist, co-owner of a Torrance urgent-care clinic and president of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified school board; endorsed by the California Nurses Association and California Federation of Teachers.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include lowering everyday costs and holding utility and insurance companies accountable, expanding access to health care, and strengthening public schools.

candidates.name: Paul Seo
candidates.bio: Mayor of Rancho Palos Verdes, deputy state attorney general, former LA County deputy district attorney and Army veteran; endorsed by outgoing Asm. Muratsuchi and Sen. Adam Schiff.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include cracking down on corruption in Sacramento, lowering the cost of living, and public safety including funding for police, sheriff's deputies and the CHP.

66.likely_winner_basis: Democrat-vs-Democrat race; Seo led the primary 26.6-24.6 and has the incumbent's endorsement, but roughly 38% of primary votes went to Republicans whose November preference is uncertain.
66.summary: Open seat (Muratsuchi termed out) with two Democrats, Rancho Palos Verdes Mayor Paul Seo and school board president Sara Deen, after a close six-way primary; the general is competitive.

candidates.name: Mark Pulido
candidates.bio: Cerritos mayor pro tem and city councilmember (2011-2020, 2025-present), former Cerritos mayor and UCLA graduate; backed by about $3.5 million in super PAC spending in the primary.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as improving local schools, supporting public safety, and increasing affordable housing and easing economic burdens on working families.

candidates.name: Paulo Morales
candidates.bio: Former Cypress police officer, Cypress city councilmember (2014-2022) and former Cypress mayor.
candidates.platform: Campaign calls for lower taxes and fees and reduced state spending, high-quality education with parental involvement, and policies to reduce crime and keep neighborhoods safe.

67.likely_winner_basis: Morales topped the primary with 31.6%, but Democratic candidates combined for about 62% of the vote in a Harris +10 district.
67.summary: Open seat (Quirk-Silva termed out) in a north Orange County/southeast LA County district; Republican Paulo Morales led a split primary but Democrat Mark Pulido is favored on combined partisan vote. Competitive.

candidates.name: Jessie Lopez
candidates.bio: Santa Ana city councilmember first elected in 2020 and re-elected in 2024; daughter of Salvadoran immigrants, backed by SEIU, other unions and the Working Families Party.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include raising wages and expanding economic opportunity, lowering health-care costs and expanding affordable housing.

candidates.name: David Penaloza
candidates.bio: Santa Ana city councilmember and businessman, lifelong district resident; endorsed by the California Democratic Party, Speaker Robert Rivas, outgoing Asm. Valencia and public-safety unions.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as controlling costs for residents, public safety and economic development.

68.likely_winner_basis: Democrat-vs-Democrat race decided by a 32.5-31.4 primary; the 29% who backed Republican Mayra Ruiz are the swing vote, which may favor the more law-enforcement-aligned Penaloza.
68.summary: Open seat (Valencia running for Senate) pitting two Santa Ana councilmembers: labor-backed Jessie Lopez against David Penaloza, who is endorsed by the state Democratic Party. Toss-up.

candidates.name: Josh Lowenthal
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2022 and Assembly Speaker pro tempore; tech and telecom entrepreneur and former teacher from Long Beach, son of former Rep. Alan Lowenthal.
candidates.platform: Committee work and campaign site emphasize job creation, consumer privacy, port infrastructure and 2028 Olympics preparation, and support for independent restaurants.

candidates.name: Carolyn Essex
candidates.bio: Legislative policy analyst and community activist who spent 18 years in civil service with the City of Los Angeles.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as reducing street homelessness, improving public safety in neighborhoods and schools, and addressing neglected infrastructure.

69.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent and Speaker pro tem took 68.6% of the primary to Essex's 28.5%.
69.summary: Safe seat for the Democratic incumbent in a Democrat-vs-Democrat general in Long Beach; Lowenthal is heavily favored for a third term.

candidates.name: Tri Ta
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2022; former Westminster mayor (first Vietnamese American elected mayor in the U.S.) and councilmember, employment counselor by profession.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as helping small businesses, smaller and more efficient government, and transportation.

candidates.name: Paula Swift
candidates.bio: Small-business owner, educator and CEO with a USC doctorate in organizational change and leadership; switched from a CA-40 congressional bid to this race after Prop 50 redistricting.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include lowering the cost of living in Orange County, public safety and thriving communities, and strong public schools.

70.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led a two-way primary 53.8-46.2 in a Trump +3 district he won with 54.7% in 2024.
70.summary: Republican incumbent Tri Ta faces Democrat Paula Swift in a Little Saigon-area district; Ta is favored but the seat is one of the more competitive Republican-held Assembly seats.

candidates.name: Kate Sanchez
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2022 and former businesswoman; vice chair of the Health and Revenue and Taxation committees.
candidates.platform: Campaign materials emphasize her committee work on health policy and taxation.

candidates.name: JJ Galvez
candidates.bio: Technology consultant and director of the Silverado-Modjeska Recreation and Park District who immigrated to California for college and lives in Silverado Canyon.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include addressing the high cost of housing and living, preparing the economy for technological change, and improving wildfire and flood resilience.

71.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led a two-way primary 58.2-41.8 in a Trump +11 district.
71.summary: Safe Republican seat spanning south Orange County and southwest Riverside County; Sanchez seeks a third term against Democrat JJ Galvez.

incumbent.name: Diane Dixon
incumbent.note: running for Orange County Board of Supervisors (District 5)

candidates.name: Chris Kluwe
candidates.bio: Former NFL punter (UCLA, Minnesota Vikings), author and community advocate from Huntington Beach.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as affordable housing in Orange County, public education and climate resiliency.

candidates.name: Gracey Van Der Mark
candidates.bio: Huntington Beach city councilmember and former mayor (the city's first Latina mayor), born to immigrant parents; endorsed by the California Republican Party.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as fiscal responsibility, parental rights and public safety.

72.likely_winner_basis: Kluwe led the primary with 43.8%, but the two Republicans combined for 54.1% in a Trump +2.7 district that Dixon won with 59.5% in 2024; lean Republican but competitive.
72.summary: Open seat (Dixon running for county supervisor) along the Orange County coast; Democrat Chris Kluwe topped the primary but faces a consolidated Republican vote behind Gracey Van Der Mark. Competitive.

candidates.name: Cottie Petrie-Norris
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2018 and chair of the Utilities and Energy Committee; Yale graduate with a 20-year career in finance and technology.
candidates.platform: Committee work and campaign materials emphasize utilities and energy policy, climate change, higher education and reproductive health.

candidates.name: Urson Russell
candidates.bio: Businessman with 30 years in operations and logistics who co-founded a lithium golf-car fleet company and a wearable-camera company and now manufactures reusable storage bags.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as election administration and government efficiency, parental rights and institutional accountability, and immigration reform.

73.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led a two-way primary 60.9-39.1 in a Harris +17 district.
73.summary: Democratic incumbent Petrie-Norris is favored for a fifth term over Republican businessman Urson Russell in an Irvine-centered district.

candidates.name: Laurie Davies
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2020; former Laguna Niguel mayor and councilmember and founder of a wedding and events company.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as keeping neighborhoods safe, keeping prices affordable for families, protecting the coastline and reducing wildfire risk.

candidates.name: Sergio Farias
candidates.bio: Three-term San Juan Capistrano city councilmember twice chosen as mayor; owned a landscaping business for nearly two decades.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include public safety and infrastructure, reducing homelessness and expanding housing affordability, and fiscal responsibility and government transparency.

74.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led the primary 52.3-47.7 and won 50.8% in 2024, but the district voted Harris +1.8; lean Republican, highly competitive.
74.summary: One of the most competitive Assembly seats in the state: Republican incumbent Davies defends a coastal south Orange County/north San Diego County district that narrowly voted for Harris against Democrat Sergio Farias.

candidates.name: Carl DeMaio
candidates.bio: First-term incumbent assemblymember, chairman of Reform California, radio/podcast host and former San Diego city councilmember.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include lowering living costs, eliminating special-interest influence and election-integrity measures.

candidates.name: Gerald Boursiquot
candidates.bio: 22-year Navy and Air Force veteran, former UAW auto worker, IT contractor and Palomar College adjunct professor from Fallbrook.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities include expanding affordable housing, reducing the cost of living and addressing insurance availability.

75.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led the primary 59.7-40.3 in a Trump +14 district.
75.summary: Safe Republican seat in inland north and east San Diego County; DeMaio seeks a second term against Democrat Gerald Boursiquot.

candidates.name: Darshana Patel
candidates.bio: First-term incumbent assemblymember and chair of the Education Committee; research scientist with a UC Irvine biophysics doctorate and former Poway Unified school board president.
candidates.platform: Priorities include addressing the cost of living, increasing public-education funding, youth mental-health access and public safety.

candidates.name: Carrie Espinoza Villanueva
candidates.bio: Academic department assistant supporting trades programs at Palomar College; raised in an agricultural family and has owned small businesses in manufacturing, diesel remanufacturing and ranch operations.
candidates.platform: Campaign calls for cutting taxes and regulations to reduce the cost of living, addressing homelessness and addiction, aligning education with job needs and protecting retirees' savings from taxation.

76.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led the primary 55.8-44.2 in a Harris +13 district she won with 54% in 2024.
76.summary: Democratic incumbent Patel is favored for a second term over Republican Carrie Espinoza Villanueva in a north San Diego County district that was competitive in 2024.

candidates.name: Tasha Boerner
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2018 (formerly Boerner Horvath) and chair of the Communications and Conveyance Committee; former Encinitas city councilmember.
candidates.platform: Priorities include reducing housing, utility and insurance costs, protecting the coastal environment and improving education funding.

candidates.name: Trinity Hannaway
candidates.bio: Executive director of the Reform California PAC and former district outreach director for Asm. Carl DeMaio.

77.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led the primary 61.8-38.2 in a Harris +29 coastal district.
77.summary: Safe Democratic coastal San Diego County seat; Boerner seeks a fifth term against Republican Trinity Hannaway, who has no public campaign website.

candidates.name: Chris Ward
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since 2020, chair of the Arts, Entertainment, Sports and Tourism Committee and former Speaker pro tempore; former San Diego city councilmember with a Harvard Kennedy School MPP.
candidates.platform: Priorities include housing affordability, consumer privacy protections from emerging technology and renewable energy.

candidates.name: Payton Galvez
candidates.bio: Field manager for the Reform California PAC and staffer in Asm. Carl DeMaio's office; ballot designation 'Constituent Services Manager'.

78.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 68.5% of the primary in a Harris +36 district.
78.summary: Safe Democratic seat in central San Diego; Ward seeks a fourth term against Republican Payton Galvez.

candidates.name: LaShae Sharp-Collins
candidates.bio: First-term incumbent assemblymember, educator and former San Diego State University instructor; serves on the Health, Appropriations and Budget committees.
candidates.platform: Priorities include protecting reproductive freedom, education equity, CalFresh enrollment and nutrition, housing affordability and addressing homelessness.

candidates.name: Andrew Lawson
candidates.bio: Lawyer, former substitute teacher and member of the Spring Valley Community Planning Group.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as housing affordability, public safety, and government accountability and transparency.

79.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led the primary 64.7-35.3 in a Harris +23 district.
79.summary: Democratic incumbent Sharp-Collins is favored for a second term over Republican Andrew Lawson in a southeastern San Diego/La Mesa/Lemon Grove district.

candidates.name: David Alvarez
candidates.bio: Incumbent assemblymember since a 2022 special election; former two-term San Diego city councilmember (District 8), 2014 mayoral candidate and founder of Causa Consulting.
candidates.platform: Campaign priorities listed as housing accessibility, education and resources, and cleaner communities.

candidates.name: Alejandro Galicia
candidates.bio: Small-business owner (principal of BPI Plumbing since 2005), military veteran and local commissioner with a UCLA linguistics degree and a master's in transportation and logistics.

80.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 59.1% of the primary in a Harris +17 district; Republican Galicia had 34.2%.
80.summary: Safe Democratic South Bay seat (Chula Vista, National City); Alvarez seeks a third full term against Republican Alejandro Galicia, who has no public campaign website.

incumbent.name: Mike McGuire
incumbent.note: termed out; running for U.S. House (CA-1)

candidates.name: Damon Connolly
candidates.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for AD-12 since 2022 and former Marin County supervisor, San Rafael city councilmember, school board president and deputy attorney general.
candidates.platform: His campaign site lists wildfire prevention, climate change and environmental protection, open space, housing, homelessness, economic revitalization, health care, transportation, reproductive rights and sustainable agriculture as priorities, citing his co-authorship of the Proposition 4 climate bond and wildfire legislation.

candidates.name: Tief Gibbs
candidates.bio: Novato small-business owner (co-owner of Vintage Vehicles) with an economics degree from San Diego State who serves on the Novato Downtown Business Association board and as secretary of the Marin Republican Central Committee; ran for Congress (CA-2) in 2024.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site lists limited government, fiscal responsibility and lower taxes, tough-on-crime public safety, parental rights in education, immigration enforcement, religious freedom, pro-life policies, Second Amendment rights, water storage and dam repair, expanded oil drilling, road repair and wildfire prevention.

2.likely_winner_basis: Won 73.4% of the primary vote in a district Harris carried 69.9-26.7.
2.summary: Open North Coast seat vacated by Senate leader Mike McGuire; Assemblymember Damon Connolly is heavily favored over Republican Tief Gibbs.

incumbent.name: Marie Alvarado-Gil
incumbent.note: ran for re-election but finished third in the primary (26.6%) and was eliminated; elected as a Democrat in 2022, switched to Republican in 2024

candidates.name: Jaron Brandon
candidates.bio: Tuolumne County supervisor since 2020 and a Sierra foothills native whose parents ran two small independent businesses.
candidates.platform: His campaign site describes a 21-area platform covering water, wildfire and insurance, housing, schools, hospitals, roads, energy and public safety, and emphasizes local control, rural issues, natural-resource management, fentanyl awareness and services for seniors and veterans.

candidates.name: Alexandra Duarte
candidates.bio: Almond farmer from Hilmar and wife of former U.S. Rep. John Duarte, running under a 'Mom. Farmer.' ballot designation.
candidates.platform: Her campaign centers on affordability: cutting gas taxes and regulations, lowering grocery costs by easing costs on farmers, insurance reform and more Cal Fire funding, forest fuel reduction, new highway lanes and job training, stricter sentencing and more law-enforcement funding, building dams and canals, and cutting taxes.

4.likely_winner_basis: Brandon led the primary, but the two Republicans combined for 58.7% and Trump carried the district 55.0-42.4; the general is competitive.
4.summary: Incumbent Marie Alvarado-Gil became the first California senator since at least 2010 to lose a primary, leaving a Sierra/Central Valley contest between Tuolumne County Supervisor Jaron Brandon (D) and almond farmer Alexandra Duarte (R). Republicans have the partisan edge but Brandon's primary plurality makes it one of the more competitive Senate races.

candidates.name: Sean Frame
candidates.bio: Small-business owner, former nine-year Placerville Union School District trustee and 2024 Assembly District 6 candidate who runs a self-described corporate-free campaign.
candidates.platform: His site lists corporate-free funding, affordable housing (including a state public bank and a ban on private-equity purchases of single-family homes), climate action through solar and storage built with union labor, living wages, redirecting school funding toward classrooms, and preserving telework for state workers.

candidates.name: Roger Niello
candidates.bio: Republican state senator since 2022, former Assemblymember and Sacramento County supervisor, and longtime auto dealer.
candidates.platform: His campaign site prioritizes cost of living (opposing new taxes, CEQA reform, lower building fees), education (merit pay, charter schools, career prep, campus safety), health care (licensing reform, medical tort caps, health savings accounts, opposition to single-payer) and addressing homelessness through conservatorship reform and mental-health and substance-abuse treatment.

6.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent took 56.2% in the primary against two Democrats combined at 43.8%; district is near-even (Trump 49.0-47.8).
6.summary: Republican incumbent Roger Niello seeks a second term in the Sacramento/Placer suburbs against Democrat Sean Frame; the district is marginal on presidential numbers but Niello won the primary comfortably.

candidates.name: Angelique Ashby
candidates.bio: Democratic state senator for District 8 since 2022, previously a 12-year Sacramento city councilmember and vice mayor, and an attorney (McGeorge School of Law).
candidates.platform: Her campaign site says she is running to fight for regional resources and statewide policy solutions for families in Sacramento and Elk Grove, listing public safety, housing, education, the economy, environment, equitable governance, the arts and women's issues including child care, universal preschool, equal pay and reproductive freedom.

candidates.name: Susan Mason
candidates.bio: Retired nurse from Elk Grove (ballot designation: Retired Nurse). No campaign website found.

8.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 68.1% in the primary in a district Harris carried 64.4-31.9.
8.summary: Democratic incumbent Angelique Ashby is heavily favored for a second term over Republican retired nurse Susan Mason in the Sacramento-based district.

incumbent.name: Aisha Wahab
incumbent.note: running for other office (U.S. House, CA-14)

candidates.name: Scott Sakakihara
candidates.bio: Union City councilmember and former vice mayor, U.S. Navy Reserve officer, attorney, vice chair of the Housing Authority of Alameda County and former Obama White House staffer.
candidates.platform: His campaign site prioritizes lowering costs of housing, health care, child care, groceries and energy; protecting immigrants, LGBTQ+ Californians, reproductive freedom and the safety net; public safety balanced with civil rights; universal health care and preschool; responsible technology regulation; and clean energy and climate action.

candidates.name: Linda Price
candidates.bio: Sunnyvale-area businesswoman who founded an organizational consultancy, did organizational-development work for the Department of Defense and has taught leadership and management at Bay Area colleges for more than 30 years.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site lists safe communities, affordable living through reduced regulation and responsible budgeting, education including the trades, small-business support, government accountability and transparency, transportation and infrastructure, housing that respects neighborhood character, and practical environmental stewardship.

10.likely_winner_basis: Democrats combined for 76.8% of the six-way primary and Harris carried the district 66.5-29.2.
10.summary: Open East Bay/Silicon Valley seat; Union City Councilmember Scott Sakakihara emerged from a crowded Democratic field and is favored over Republican Linda Price, who advanced as the only Republican.

incumbent.name: Shannon Grove
incumbent.note: termed out; running for State Board of Equalization

candidates.name: Nathan Magsig
candidates.bio: Fresno County supervisor (District 5, elected 2016), former Clovis mayor and city councilmember, and licensed general contractor who has also worked as a legislative aide and nonprofit affordable-housing director.
candidates.platform: His campaign site lists oil and agricultural production, public safety and wildfire reduction as top priorities, pledging to curb state spending and return local control, loosen water regulations for farmers, oppose policies he calls anti-law-enforcement, and pursue forest management aimed at lowering insurance costs.

candidates.name: William Brown Jr.
candidates.bio: Clinical social worker, Marine veteran and Visalia resident running as a Libertarian; previously a candidate in the 2025 Assembly District 32 special election.
candidates.platform: His campaign emphasizes lower taxes, fewer regulations and individual choice, citing opposition to AB 5's independent-contractor rules, support for more in-state oil production and criticism of state insurance rate caps.

12.likely_winner_basis: Won 59.5% of the primary; no Democrat filed, and Trump carried the district 61.7-35.9.
12.summary: Open Kern/Tulare/eastern Fresno seat with no Democrat on the ballot; Fresno County Supervisor Nathan Magsig (R) faces Libertarian social worker William Brown Jr. and is the clear favorite.

incumbent.name: Anna Caballero
incumbent.note: termed out; running for State Treasurer

candidates.name: Esmeralda Soria
candidates.bio: State Assemblymember (AD-27, since 2022), former Fresno city councilmember, and former educator and attorney who grew up as the daughter of Central Valley farmworkers.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site says she is fighting for working families, affordable housing, health-care access and economic opportunity in the Central Valley.

candidates.name: Darin DuPont
candidates.bio: Merced city councilmember since 2024 and water attorney (ballot designation 'Councilman/Water Attorney').
candidates.platform: His campaign centers on the affordability crisis for Central Valley families, calling for cutting gas taxes, opposing tax increases and unfunded mandates and stopping refinery shutdowns; he also lists water security (expanding storage), holding the High-Speed Rail Authority accountable and ending one-party control in Sacramento.

14.likely_winner_basis: Democrats combined for 59.6% of the primary and Harris narrowly carried the district 50.7-46.7, but DuPont's 40.4% keeps it competitive.
14.summary: Open western Central Valley seat; Assemblymember Esmeralda Soria (D) is favored over Merced Councilmember Darin DuPont (R) in a swing-leaning district with low primary turnout.

candidates.name: Melissa Hurtado
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator since 2018 and the daughter of Central Valley farmworkers; previously a Sanger city councilmember.
candidates.platform: Her campaign highlights lowering costs of gas, groceries and utilities by combating what she describes as corporate price-fixing, cutting red tape to build affordable housing, investing in water infrastructure for farms, fully funding local law enforcement and addiction treatment, expanding health-care access and funding public schools.

candidates.name: Guillermo Gonzalez
candidates.bio: Republican congressional aide and small-business owner from the Central Valley, endorsed by Reps. David Valadao and Vince Fong, the Kern County Farm Bureau and the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC.
candidates.platform: His 'Valley Promise' plan proposes ending the state gasoline tax, eliminating state income tax on the first $150,000 of income and a $500 state grocery tax credit, along with cutting red tape for small business and agriculture, building affordable homes, improving public safety and local access to doctors.

16.likely_winner_basis: Toss-up: Republican Gonzalez led the primary 45.2-35.6 and Trump carried the district 53.2-44.3, but the two Democrats combined for 54.8% and Hurtado has twice won here.
16.summary: Two-term Democratic incumbent Melissa Hurtado, who won re-election in 2022 by 20 votes, trails Republican Guillermo Gonzalez after the primary in a Trump-won Central Valley district; this is the likeliest Republican pickup.

candidates.name: Steve Padilla
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator since 2022, former Chula Vista mayor and city councilmember, former Chula Vista police detective and former chair of the California Coastal Commission.
candidates.platform: His campaign frames its agenda as 'rebuilding opportunity': economic recovery and tackling income inequality in South County and Imperial County, expanding health-care access, strengthening public education, climate leadership and combating racial injustice; recent items highlight his bills on data-center utility costs and AI therapy chatbots.

candidates.name: Art Hodges
candidates.bio: Pastor and bishop who, according to his campaign, oversees about 350 churches in Southern California, previously worked as a school principal and college chancellor, and led litigation against California's COVID-era restrictions on houses of worship.
candidates.platform: Under the slogan 'Faith, Family, Freedom, Future,' his priorities are affordability (housing, gas and utility costs, taxes and insurance), border-related issues including Tijuana River sewage pollution, restricting transgender participation in girls' sports, parental rights in school curriculum and health decisions, and reducing government fraud and waste.

18.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 63.8% in the two-candidate primary; Harris carried the district 55.3-42.2.
18.summary: Democratic incumbent Steve Padilla is favored for a second term over Republican pastor Art Hodges in the South Bay San Diego/Imperial Valley district.

candidates.name: Caroline Menjivar
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator for District 20 since 2022, Marine Corps veteran, former EMT and social worker.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site says she is fighting for working families, housing solutions and public services, drawing on her own experience with housing instability.

candidates.name: Tony Rodriguez
candidates.bio: Republican candidate; filed with no ballot designation and no active campaign website.

20.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 62.1% in the primary in a district Harris carried 62.4-34.4.
20.summary: Democratic incumbent Caroline Menjivar is heavily favored over Republican Tony Rodriguez in the San Fernando Valley district.

candidates.name: Susan Rubio
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator since 2018, former public-school teacher and Baldwin Park city councilmember.
candidates.platform: Her campaign site is organized around her record, highlighting work on affordable housing and homelessness, the environment, ending domestic violence, education, protecting women, wildfire, nonprofits and small-business advocacy.

candidates.name: Mike Netter
candidates.bio: San Gabriel Valley small-business owner and self-described advocate who has not held elected office.
candidates.platform: His stated priorities are lowering energy and electricity costs and opposing state electrification mandates, reducing taxes, improving public safety and addressing crime and homelessness, and lowering the cost of living.

22.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 62.3% in the primary; Harris carried the district 55.6-41.5.
22.summary: Two-term Democratic incumbent Susan Rubio is favored over Republican small-business owner Mike Netter in the San Gabriel/Pomona Valley district.

incumbent.name: Ben Allen
incumbent.note: termed out; running for Insurance Commissioner

candidates.name: John Erickson
candidates.bio: West Hollywood city councilmember (since 2020) and former mayor, chief of staff at the Alliance for a Better Community and former vice president at Planned Parenthood Los Angeles.
candidates.platform: He emphasizes affordability and state revenue reform, renter protections including Ellis Act and Costa-Hawkins reform, housing-first homelessness programs, wildfire rebuilding and insurance availability, gun control, single-payer health care and climate action; relative to Goldsmith he leans more on renter protections and single-payer.

candidates.name: Brian Goldsmith
candidates.bio: West Los Angeles business owner, lawyer and former political journalist/producer who launched two tech startups and worked on Democratic campaigns.
candidates.platform: Runs on 'Safety. Affordability. Results.': permitting and regulatory reform to make it cheaper to live and do business, more workforce housing and clean-energy transmission, taking on crime and homelessness (he supported Prop 36), school and insurance reform, and combating antisemitism and hate; relative to Erickson he emphasizes public safety and is endorsed by the LA Police Protective League and DA Nathan Hochman.

24.likely_winner_basis: Democrat-vs-Democrat general after a 10-candidate primary in which Erickson led Goldsmith by only 2.2 points; outcome depends on how the 31.6% who backed the two eliminated Republicans break.
24.summary: Open Westside/South Bay LA seat; West Hollywood Councilmember John Erickson and business owner Brian Goldsmith, both Democrats, advanced from a crowded primary in which the two Republicans were squeezed out. The seat stays Democratic regardless.

incumbent.name: María Elena Durazo
incumbent.note: running for other office (Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors)

candidates.name: Sara Hernandez
candidates.bio: Los Angeles Community College District trustee and affordable-housing advocate; a former teacher, lawyer and nonprofit executive director.
candidates.platform: Her priorities are building more housing, expanding public transit, debt-free higher education and good-paying jobs, safe and walkable neighborhoods, green space and universal childcare, keeping film and TV production in Los Angeles, and protecting immigrant communities.

candidates.name: Sarah Rascón
candidates.bio: Native Angeleno and former director of county and regional affairs for Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass (ballot designation 'Environmental Protection Director').
candidates.platform: Her listed priorities are environmental and social justice, housing access and affordability, workforce development, children and family welfare, small businesses and the entertainment industry, health care, immigration, corporate accountability and gun safety; she is endorsed by outgoing Sen. María Elena Durazo.

26.likely_winner_basis: Led the eight-candidate primary by nearly 12 points (31.2% to 19.4%).
26.summary: Open central/east LA seat with a Democrat-vs-Democrat general between LA Community College District trustee Sara Hernandez and former Bass administration official Sarah Rascón; former Assemblymember Wendy Carrillo finished third. The seat stays Democratic.

candidates.name: Lola Smallwood-Cuevas
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator since 2022 and chair of the Senate Labor Committee; former journalist, SEIU organizer, co-founder of the LA Black Worker Center and UCLA Labor Center project director.
candidates.platform: She is running on jobs and labor protections (citing her Equal Pay and Anti-Retaliation Act and wage-theft bills), homelessness and affordable-housing production, universal health care, community safety, environmental justice and anti-displacement economic development.

candidates.name: Joe Lisuzzo
candidates.bio: Los Angeles restaurant and food-manufacturing business owner of 32 years (Al Gelato) and neighborhood councilmember.
candidates.platform: His priorities are ending 'waste, fraud and abuse,' increasing public-safety funding, addressing homelessness, cutting business taxes and regulation, education reform including alternative schools, veterans' services, infrastructure repair and a gas-tax holiday.

28.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 77.5% in the primary in the most Democratic district on the ballot (Harris 78.4-18.4).
28.summary: Democratic incumbent Lola Smallwood-Cuevas is a near-certain winner over Republican restaurant owner Joe Lisuzzo in the downtown/South LA district.

candidates.name: Bob Archuleta
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator since 2018, U.S. Army veteran (82nd Airborne), former Montebello reserve police officer, former Pico Rivera councilmember and mayor, and chair of the Senate Military and Veterans Affairs Committee.
candidates.platform: His re-election site emphasizes his record and continued focus on economic growth and small business, education funding, environmental protection and clean energy, expanding health-care access, public safety and emergency preparedness, and veterans' services.

candidates.name: Araceli Martinez
candidates.bio: Small-business owner, UC Riverside graduate and former journalist and political analyst; the daughter of immigrants from Mexico and Honduras.
candidates.platform: Her stated priorities are affordability through lower taxes and less regulation, cutting red tape for small businesses, parental rights, and public safety including supporting law enforcement and holding repeat offenders accountable.

30.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 65.1% in the two-candidate primary; Harris carried the district 57.1-39.8.
30.summary: Two-term Democratic incumbent Bob Archuleta is favored over Republican small-business owner Araceli Martinez in the Gateway Cities district.

candidates.name: Tiffanie Tate
candidates.bio: Physician (obstetrician-gynecologist), educator and author; first-time candidate.
candidates.platform: Her site lists relief from rising costs, safe and affordable health care, job creation and workers' rights, support and accountability for schools, community safety, and responsible budgeting and transparency.

candidates.name: Kelly Seyarto
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator since 2022, former Assemblymember (2020-22), retired Los Angeles County Fire Department battalion chief and four-time Murrieta mayor.
candidates.platform: His campaign emphasizes public safety (he authored bills creating the state Fentanyl Task Force and real-time overdose tracking), support for veterans and military families, and government accountability, saying he wants to 'make California the Golden State once again.'

32.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent won 58.2% in the two-candidate primary; Trump carried the district 56.1-41.0.
32.summary: Republican incumbent Kelly Seyarto is favored for a second term over Democratic physician Tiffanie Tate in the southwest Riverside County-based district.

incumbent.name: Tom Umberg
incumbent.note: termed out; running for State Board of Equalization

candidates.name: Avelino Valencia
candidates.bio: State Assemblymember for AD-68 since 2022, former Anaheim city councilmember and son of immigrant small-business owners.
candidates.platform: He says he will fully fund schools, curb rising costs, build housing and expand first-time-homebuyer programs, combat climate change, create good-paying jobs, increase government transparency and expand health coverage.

candidates.name: Rhonda Shader
candidates.bio: Small-business owner, former Placentia city councilmember and two-time mayor; the 2022 runner-up in this district.
candidates.platform: Runs on a '10-point business plan': lower taxes, infrastructure public-private partnerships, cutting state waste and regulation, school choice, streamlined licensing, lower health-care costs and PAGA lawsuit reform.

34.likely_winner_basis: Won 65.2% of the two-candidate primary; Harris carried the district 56.6-40.3.
34.summary: Open north Orange County seat; Assemblymember Avelino Valencia (D) is favored over former Placentia Mayor Rhonda Shader (R), the 2022 runner-up here.

candidates.name: Chris Duncan
candidates.bio: Attorney and former federal prosecutor who served as San Clemente mayor and on the Orange County Fire Authority board; twice ran for AD-74 (ballot designation 'Anti-Tariff Attorney').
candidates.platform: Says he will make California more affordable, cut red tape, fight for the region's fair share of state funding, keep neighborhoods safe and hold Sacramento accountable; highlights his litigation against federal tariffs and emphasizes ethics and anti-corruption.

candidates.name: Tony Strickland
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator, elected in a 2025 special election; previously served in the Assembly and Senate and as mayor of Huntington Beach.
candidates.platform: Campaigns on making California more affordable: letting taxpayers keep more of their money, cutting waste and lowering costs, keeping communities safe and election integrity; cites a lifetime 'A' rating from the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association.

36.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led the two-candidate primary 53.4-46.6 and Trump carried the district 50.6-46.6, but the margin makes this competitive.
36.summary: Republican incumbent Tony Strickland, elected in a 2025 special election, faces former San Clemente Mayor Chris Duncan (D) in coastal Orange County; one of the few genuinely competitive Senate races and a Democratic target.

candidates.name: Catherine Blakespear
candidates.bio: Incumbent state senator since 2022 and former three-term Encinitas mayor and councilmember.
candidates.platform: Seeks re-election on lowering costs of childcare, insurance and housing, cutting red tape for interim housing to address homelessness, climate resiliency, gun safety, transit, and protecting open space and beaches; cites 24 bills signed in her first term.

candidates.name: Laura Bassett
candidates.bio: Lifelong Oceanside resident, licensed professional fiduciary and real-estate professional, owner of two local businesses and a San Diego County Civil Service Commissioner.
candidates.platform: Campaign themes are 'Safe. Strong. Affordable.': reining in state spending and new taxes, removing barriers to housing construction, restoring North County beaches and a balanced approach to public safety.

38.likely_winner_basis: Incumbent led the two-candidate primary 54.7-45.3; Harris carried the district 54.9-42.1.
38.summary: Democratic incumbent Catherine Blakespear is favored for a second term over Republican fiduciary Laura Bassett in the coastal North County San Diego/south Orange County district, though the margin is moderate.

candidates.name: Mara Elliott
candidates.bio: Ethics attorney who served two terms as San Diego City Attorney (2016-2024), the first woman and first Latina in the office.
candidates.platform: Priorities listed are affordability (housing, health care, small-business support), public safety (gun-violence prevention, domestic-violence and senior protections, mental-health response) and making government work smarter through fiscal accountability.

candidates.name: Kristie Bruce-Lane
candidates.bio: Businesswoman with a career in agriculture and health care, victims' advocate and former Olivenhain Municipal Water District board member; twice the runner-up for AD-76.
candidates.platform: Says she will reduce the cost of living and cut taxes, address homelessness, keep communities safe, restore excellence in education, confront the fentanyl crisis and work for a clean environment.

40.likely_winner_basis: Toss-up: Elliott won 48.0% of the primary but the two Republicans combined for 52.1%; Harris carried the district 50.4-46.7.
40.summary: Open inland San Diego County seat vacated by termed-out Republican leader Brian Jones; former San Diego City Attorney Mara Elliott (D) faces businesswoman Kristie Bruce-Lane (R). Combined primary votes favor Republicans, presidential numbers favor Democrats, making it a top pickup opportunity for Democrats.
